rationale:
OWNER DECISION 1, 2026-08-18: 'do not switch the handler off for this — write something other than failed'.

THE PROBLEM, plainly. A page whose pages.rebuild_policy is 'owned' belongs to a tool or widget. The owned-page guard in SavePageSectionsAction refuses a generic section save over it, because that save DELETEs and reinserts every page_component and would clobber the live tool. Refusing is correct and is not in question. What is wrong is what the refused work item then RECORDS: it dies `failed`, the same word used for a handler that tried the job and could not do it.

THE RULE THAT MAKES THAT EXPENSIVE. scheduled_tasks.detected-item-promoter (SCH-026; migration 444, corrected by 454 and 465) refuses to dispatch an (item_type, handler_agent) pair whose lifetime successes are under 25% of its terminal outcomes once there are >= 5 of them. Read from the LIVE pre_query on 2026-08-18, that floor is computed over exactly two buckets — c = count FILTER (status IN ('complete','verified')) and f = count FILTER (status = 'failed') — and it names no other status.

HOW THIS CASE MEASURES AGAINST IT. Every ownership refusal is therefore a vote in a competence measure it says nothing about. phantom_internal_link -> page-build-handler is the live illustration: 101 ok / 46 failed = 69% on GENERIC pages, and 0 ok / 14 failed on OWNED ones — not a handler doing badly, a handler never permitted to start. Blended it reads 47%, above the floor today only because its owned rows are a minority. ~134 non-terminal findings sit behind this refusal on owned pages now. When a pair crosses the floor the promoter stops dispatching that item_type ENTIRELY, including the 69% of findings on generic pages that were being repaired. With `wont_fix` the pair reads NEVER TESTED HERE, which is the truth: wont_fix is in neither bucket, so the refusal leaves numerator and denominator alone.

WHY THE CHANGE HAS THE SHAPE IT HAS. An action cannot name its own error step (coordinator.go routeToErrorStep takes a static config value), and a typed Go error does not cross the action -> coordinator -> error_step boundary. The ONLY channel that survives is collected_data.__step_error.message, which routeToErrorStep copies verbatim from the action's error. So the refusal is made machine-identifiable by leading that error with ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix, and the routed step reads it. Scoping to that marker is the load-bearing part: a genuine save failure (shrink guard, banned claim) on the same step still records `failed` and still counts, or the floor would go blind to real incompetence — which is worse than the bug being fixed.

WHY AN OPT-IN FIELD RATHER THAN A RULE IN CODE. Owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2: new authority on a shared seam ships as an opt-in field whose UNSAFE side is the default, so the decision is visible to a reviewer of the CALLER. owned_page_refusal_status is absent everywhere and inert everywhere until a migration names it; one migration (480) names exactly one step.

CONSUMERS, ENUMERATED RATHER THAN ASSERTED (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §3). The refusal can reach a work-item status write only from save_page_sections. Every live agent with such a step, queried 2026-08-18: page-build-handler save_sections -> mark_item_failed (update_work_item_status — this one); page-rerender save_sections -> no error_step at all; tool-recreation-handler save_sections -> complete_error, which runs complete_workflow and writes no item status. One applicable consumer.

BLAST RADIUS OF THE STATUS ITSELF, measured not assumed. Of the consumers that read wont_fix positively: silentCoverageClause (diagnose_silent_check_action.go) treats failed and wont_fix alike; crossLinkFailedStatuses lists both; check_page_canonical_collision's suppression is scoped to its own item_type. No scheduled_task pre_query mentions wont_fix at all. Only retraction differs — workItemClosedStatuses holds wont_fix and not failed, so such a row will not later be retracted, which is correct for a row that is already closed. idx_swi_dedup excludes BOTH, so the dedup key is released either way and the finding re-raises when detected again.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated because it is the obvious objection. It does not repair a single owned page. The repair route (section-editor / apply_section_edit, 220 complete / 5 failed = 98% on owned pages) exists and works; nothing converts a detector's finding into its field_updates payload. That is Tier 2, is architecture-scope, and gets an RFC. This is Tier 1: stop a routing defect from switching off a 69%-effective repair path for findings that have nothing to do with it.

plan.summary: An owned-page refusal is recorded as `failed`, and a fleet-wide dispatch gate counts `failed`. The detected-item-promoter holds any (item_type, handler_agent) pair whose lifetime successes fall under 25% of complete+verified+failed, and it names no other status — so a routing refusal, which says nothing about the handler's competence, votes against it and can switch the pair off entirely, including on the generic pages where it was working (phantom_internal_link: 69% generic, 0/14 owned). This change makes SavePageSectionsAction's refusal error carry the estate's existing ownership marker, and adds ONE opt-in config key to update_work_item_status — owned_page_refusal_status, absent and therefore inert everywhere — which records that status instead when the routed step error carries the marker. A genuine save failure on the same step still records `failed` and still counts. Migration 480 opts exactly one step in (page-build-handler.mark_item_failed -> wont_fix); it is applied and ledger-recorded, and is inert on the current binary because nothing reads the key until the Go half rolls.

edits.rationale: Make the ownership refusal machine-identifiable at the only place its terminal status is chosen. routeToErrorStep copies the error message verbatim into __step_error.message; without a marker in it, an ownership refusal and a shrink-guard failure are the same string to the routed step. Uses the estate's existing single ownership token rather than inventing a second one.
edits.sketch:
@@ owned-page guard, the refusal return @@
-			return nil, fmt.Errorf(
-				"page %s is rebuild_policy=owned (tool/widget-owned): a generic section save "+
+			// The error LEADS with ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix (owner decision 1,
+			// 2026-08-18). routeToErrorStep copies this message verbatim into
+			// collected_data.__step_error.message, which is the only channel that
+			// survives the action -> coordinator -> error_step boundary.

 					"would clobber it. Use apply_section_edit for targeted edits or the tool "+
 					"pipeline for rebuilds. Refusing to overwrite.",
-				pageName)

edits.rationale: The opt-in itself, on UpdateWorkItemStatusAction. Absent -> inert -> today's behaviour for every caller (the unsafe default is OFF, per the 2026-08-02 §2 ruling). Present AND the routed error carries the ownership marker -> record the refusal status instead. Scoped to the marker so a genuine save failure still counts in the promoter's floor. Validated against the SAME validStatuses map as `status`, because two vocabularies for one column is the drift class this estate keeps filing bugs about.

Correct a stale doc comment that is now dangerous. It read 'It is matched by nothing — the skip protocol is a boolean', which was already false when written (two call sites match it in a skip_reason) and is now false in a third and higher-stakes way: the literal decides a work item's terminal STATUS. A future edit that renames it on the strength of that comment would silently switch the substitution off. The full matcher set is listed so the next reader can see what a rename costs.
edits.sketch:
-// ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix marks a skip caused by this guard. It is matched by
-// nothing — the skip protocol is a boolean — but it is the string to pod-grep ...
+// ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix marks a refusal caused by this guard. ...
+// > **CORRECTED 2026-08-18:** this comment used to say "It is matched by nothing".
+// > ... The full matcher set, so a future edit knows what it would break:
+// >	 SavePageSectionsAction     — an upstream skip_reason, and its own error
+// >	 UpdatePageStatusAction     — an upstream skip_reason (refuses the 'deployed' stamp)
+// >	 UpdateWorkItemStatusAction — __step_error.message (chooses the terminal status)
+// > Changing this literal changes an item's terminal STATUS, not only a log line.
 const ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix = "OWNED_PAGE_GUARD"

edits.rationale: Four assertions that are a SET, not a list. The downgrade alone proves nothing — a rule firing on everything would pass it. The default-OFF case and the genuine-save-failure case are what show the field discriminates. Mutation-proven in both directions before submitting: making the marker never match fails the downgrade assertion; making it always match fails the default-OFF and genuine-failure assertions. Also adds captureTextArg, because the result payload reaches the driver as []byte and the existing captureArg records "" for it — every JSONB assertion would otherwise pass vacuously against an empty string.

The config half: the single deliberate opt-in. Guarded on the live step's shape (exactly one live row; action is update_work_item_status; status is still 'failed'; the key is not already set; save_sections actually routes its error HERE, or the field would sit on a step the refusal never reaches and the migration would look applied and do nothing). Verify is a DO/RAISE block, not SELECTs — ON_ERROR_STOP does not fire on a non-empty result set — and carries a negative control asserting no OTHER live step acquired the key, without which the positive assertion would pass identically on an UPDATE with no WHERE clause. Exercised end to end before applying: dry run in a transaction that rolled back, plus two probes proving the already-set guard and the leak control each abort.
edits.sketch:
UPDATE agent_definitions
   SET default_config = jsonb_set(default_config,
           '{workflow,steps,mark_item_failed,config,owned_page_refusal_status}',
           '"wont_fix"'::jsonb, true)
 WHERE type = 'page-build-handler' AND is_active
   AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL;

edits.rationale: Removes the key and asserts the rest of the step survived (a #- on the wrong path would otherwise look like a clean rollback). Deliberately does NOT rewrite rows already written wont_fix back to failed: they are a true record of a refusal that happened, and rewriting them would re-inject exactly the false votes 480 removed. Names the query that finds them (result ? 'owned_page_refusal') for anyone who disagrees.

grounded_in: LIVE scheduled_tasks.detected-item-promoter pre_query, read 2026-08-18: "SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE h.status IN ('complete', 'verified')) AS c, count(*) FILTER (WHERE h.status = 'failed') AS f" and "SELECT (c + f) < 5 OR c >= 0.25 * (c + f)" — the floor names no status other than complete/verified/failed.

LIVE pg_indexes idx_swi_dedup, read 2026-08-18: "WHERE ((item_key IS NOT NULL) AND (status <> ALL (ARRAY['complete','verified','rejected','wont_fix','failed','unresolved','cancelled'])))" — both failed and wont_fix release the dedup key.

coordinator.go routeToErrorStep: "state.CollectedData[\"__step_error\"] = map[string]interface{}{ \"failed_step\": failedStepName, \"message\": errorMsg }" — the action's error message, verbatim, is the only thing that crosses to the error step.

LIVE agent_definitions page-build-handler mark_item_failed, read 2026-08-18: {"action": "update_work_item_status", "config": {"status": "failed", "skip_if_missing": true, "work_item_id_field": "input_data.work_item_id"}} — an unconditional failed.

LIVE agent_definitions, every live step whose action is save_page_sections, read 2026-08-18: page-build-handler.save_sections -> mark_item_failed; page-rerender.save_sections -> (no error_step); tool-recreation-handler.save_sections -> complete_error (action complete_workflow).

bugs_open/301 contribution, terminal outcomes over site_work_items UNION ALL site_work_items_archive joined to pages.rebuild_policy: phantom_internal_link 101 ok / 46 failed = 69% on generic pages against 0 ok / 14 failed on owned pages; five MODIFY-shaped types are 0 of 39 on owned pages while five ADD-shaped types are 74 ok.

work_items_common.go workItemClosedStatuses comment: "closed (retraction): complete verified rejected wont_fix cancelled" — the single behavioural difference between failed and wont_fix that this change relies on being acceptable.
plan.risks:
1. The status substitution is keyed on a STRING MARKER in __step_error.message, because an action cannot name its own error step and a typed error does not survive the coordinator boundary. If someone renames ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix, refusals silently go back to `failed`. Mitigated by the corrected doc comment listing all three matchers and by the test building its fixture FROM the constant, so a rename breaks the test rather than production. A reviewer should say whether a marker is acceptable here or whether the coordinator should carry structured error metadata instead — that is the wider fix and it is not in this change.

2. `wont_fix` differs from `failed` in exactly one consumer: workItemClosedStatuses (retraction) holds wont_fix and not failed, so these rows will never be retracted. Argued as correct for an already-closed row. A reviewer should check whether any consumer this lane did not find reads wont_fix as 'a HUMAN ruled on this' — check_page_canonical_collision does, but scoped to its own item_type.

3. It narrows what the promoter's floor can see. That is the intent, but it means an owned-page refusal no longer shows up as a failure anywhere the floor looks. The visibility channel is the owned_page_review row that bugs_closed/295 already files, plus result->'owned_page_refusal' on the item. A reviewer should check that is enough, because the alternative reading is that this hides a real routing defect.

4. It repairs nothing. ~134 findings stay queued on owned pages; the detector->editor routing (Tier 2) is architecture-scope and gets an RFC. If a reviewer thinks Tier 1 makes Tier 2 less likely to be built, say so.

5. Coordination: bugs_open/301's author is reordering the SAME guard in the same week (moving it earlier so the LLM writer does not run first). These changes compose — an earlier refusal still terminates the item and still needs to write something other than failed — but a reviewer should confirm the marker survives whatever step 301 moves the refusal to.
